elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Revised 13.2 reads "Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reasons by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array". The gating trigger ("Commencing on the later of (i) [*] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product... or (ii) [*] of the... Encorafenib Product") is deleted, so the right is unconditional. The element is disjunctive (Agreement or Order Form) and this licence agreement has no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a phrase-matching artefact (the clause says "for any reasons"/"without Cause" rather than the literal words "for convenience"); in substance an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array" replaces the redacted [ * ] figure, fixing notice at exactly the preferred 30 days in writing. The retained requirement that the notice "be accompanied by the rationale for such termination" is a formality, not an additional substantive condition or consent gate.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "and Array shall refund to Ono on a pro rata basis any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination." This states the pro-rata basis expressly (not merely a post-termination-period refund) and runs from Vendor (Array) to Customer (Ono) on this specific convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Array's termination rights in the rendered Article 13 are cause-based only: 13.3 (material breach with 90/60-day cure) and 13.4 (bankruptcy/insolvency of the other Party). 13.2 is captioned "Termination by Ono without Cause" and grants the at-will right to Ono alone; no Array at-will exit appears anywhere in the rendered text, so the element is satisfied by the existing architecture without a confirming sentence. Residual note: Section 13.5 is referenced but not rendered — if it contains any Array election to terminate, this element would need revisiting.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Operative notice is "thirty (30) days' advance written notice", which is below the 60–90 day fallback band. This is a better-than-fallback outcome for Customer, not a defect, but the fallback checklist is literally unmet; the comment's offer of 60–90 days is only a negotiating position, not operative language.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: revised 13.2 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty, instalment or contingent payment on Ono's exit — it instead requires a refund to Ono. With no fee mechanic anywhere in the edited clause, the three-month cap has nothing to bite on and the element is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Array holds no convenience termination right at all under 13.2–13.4 (breach and bankruptcy only), so there is no mid-term Vendor exit to confine to term end.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Array has no convenience termination right, so no Vendor convenience notice period is required. (Array's breach termination under 13.3 already carries a 90-day cure/notice period in any event.)

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (unconditional Ono right, 30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and no Array convenience right in Article 13).

The finding classification as a deviation is sound: pre-edit, 13.2 deferred Ono's only at-will exit until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both Products under a multi-year Product-by-Product/country-by-country term (13.1), leaving no Customer convenience exit through the entire development and pre-launch period, and the notice figure was redacted — walk-away territory under T4C.

Minimality holds. The edit touches only 13.2 and only the three things the preferred checklist requires: it deletes the commencement gate (replacing it with "at any time"), fixes the redacted notice at thirty (30) days, and adds the pro-rata refund. It retains the favourable/neutral existing language verbatim ("for any reasons", "accompanied by the rationale for such termination") and leaves 13.1, 13.3 and 13.4 untouched. No survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or other model-language extra was imported, and the model clause's surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly omitted since this agreement has no Order Form or partial-termination structure.

Intent is preserved. The refund is confined to "fees prepaid... for the period after the effective date of such termination", so it does not reach the non-refundable upfront licence fee under 6.1 or non-period milestone payments; no cross-reference is broken and no retained sentence is contradicted. The Article 13 caption "Termination by Ono without Cause" remains accurate.

Substantive read of the failed deterministic check: "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a lexical miss only — the clause grants an unconditional Customer election to terminate "at any time, for any reasons", which the rule boundaries treat as a convenience right. The other three gates pass.

Residual item for the drafter (not an element failure): Section 13.5 is referenced in the rationale but not rendered. Confirm it contains no Array at-will exit; if it does, add an express carve-out so the fourth preferred element is not undermined.

Second residual item (not an element failure): the Section 8.2 Competing Product tail keys a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit "during the Initial Royalty Term". Because the exit is now available from the Effective Date rather than only post-launch, that tail can now be triggered far earlier; consider raising it separately rather than expanding this redline, since fixing it here would breach minimality.
